annotations.name: Generic EC access gate
annotations.description: Boolean gate for generic EC transfers. It does not pause the normal thermal worker.
notes: The generic access gate does not pause or acquire normal firmware bus clients.
Class 00/04 value 5 sets this gate and application state without draining or pausing normal bus clients.

annotations.name: Pending thermal work
annotations.description: Shared pending-bit mask. Failed normal transfers can remain queued for retry.
notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation, not an EC register address or an admitted host access operation.

bits.name: Manual-state write pending
bits.description: Writes EC index 36. Successful completion clears this bit and sets bit 16; it does not itself set manual-readback bit 18.

bits.name: Parameter-group reads pending
bits.description: Reads EC indices DC, 78, DE, 79, DD and DF. Successful manual write sets this bit with 2 << 15.

bits.name: Manual-state read pending
bits.description: Independently reads EC index 36 into the cached manual byte; distinct from bit 16.

annotations.name: Queued-work countdown
annotations.description: Countdown checked before queued work. It is separate from telemetry refresh timing.

annotations.name: Periodic-work countdown
annotations.description: Periodic work can enqueue new reads, so an empty queue is not a durable pause.

annotations.name: Telemetry countdown
annotations.description: Separate telemetry refresh countdown. Value 50 after a manual write is not its readback delay.

annotations.name: Shared I2C transfer status
annotations.description: Used by normal and generic transfer helpers. A generic outer success can still contain a bus failure.
notes: Shared by thermal and non-EC peripheral work; observing a status value does not acquire an ownership interval.

annotations.name: Thermal cache active marker
annotations.description: Worker initializes or services its cache based on this marker; not a host lease.

annotations.name: Cached thermal mode
annotations.description: Shared by host intent and independent EC reads. Ordinary GET can echo intent before transfer completion.

annotations.name: Cached manual flags
annotations.description: Shared requested/read state for normal manual control.

annotations.name: Cached fan 1 target
annotations.description: Shared requested/read target. Normal target GET does not synchronously read the EC.

annotations.name: Cached fan 2 target
annotations.description: Shared requested/read target. No live value is present in the image.

annotations.name: Command report ready
annotations.description: USB report handling marks a command ready; the timer-dispatched handler consumes this flag. It is not a bus-idle or completion token.
notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation; no host-readable EC register mapping is implied.

annotations.name: USB configuration value
annotations.description: USB configuration getter/setter state. Nonzero permits the timer command-processing block subject to other gates; it does not pause normal bus workers.
notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation; no host-readable EC register mapping is implied.

annotations.name: USB lifecycle flags
annotations.description: Bit 3 set is necessary for initial entry to the reviewed main-loop parking path; timer generic dispatch instead needs bit 3 clear or application state 3. These gates do not acquire the shared transfer descriptor.

references.label: Main-loop parking tests the same USB status bit

notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation; no host-readable EC register mapping is implied.

annotations.name: Application state
annotations.description: Class 00/04 stores the full payload byte before comparisons with 1, 5 and 2; no 0..5 range restriction is established. State 3 bypasses the timer USB-status gate but excludes initial entry to the reviewed main-loop parking path. Complete external mode meanings remain unresolved.

references.label: USB reset path clears application state
Decoded startup zero run covers application state

notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation; no host-readable EC register mapping is implied.
GET 00/84 returns the sampled state byte; it is not a transport-drain acknowledgment. Value 1 reaches a nonreturning MCU reset path.

Value 5 opens generic access; other returning values clear that gate. Value 2, entry to 3 and the transition from 3 to 0 also change auxiliary fields. Replaying the old byte does not establish exact restoration.
Three explicit store sites and decoded startup initialization are recovered. Bounded alias scanning does not prove absence of computed, bulk, interprocedural or unrecovered writers.

annotations.name: Initialization phase
annotations.description: Startup assigns phases 1, 2 and 3; timer command work requires at least 3. This is not a per-transfer lease.
notes: Internal MCU RAM annotation; no host-readable EC register mapping is implied.

findings.title: The named duty API is rejected
findings.description: The actual duty setter/getter wrappers reach unsupported handling in this MCU; generic register access is a separate interface.

references.label: The named duty API is rejected

findings.title: Two response status layers
findings.description: Generic register handlers store bus status separately from outer report status. Failed reads leave the supplied data area unchanged.

findings.title: Shared transfer state
findings.description: Normal main-loop work and timer-dispatched generic transfers share bus state and buffers. Full reentrancy and exclusive access are not established. The transport wait feeds a watchdog helper that re-enables interrupts, so blanket interrupt masking is not an established ownership guarantee.

findings.title: A running watchdog is not a host-loss lease
findings.description: The MCU main loop continues feeding its watchdog after host-process loss. No independent bounded fan handback is established.

references.label: A running watchdog is not a host-loss lease

findings.title: Manual write does not enqueue its own flag readback
findings.description: The successful manual-write branch sets bit 16 for a separate parameter group; index 36 readback uses bit 18. A cached GET therefore cannot be treated as confirmation of that bus write.

findings.title: Transport clients extend beyond the thermal worker
findings.description: The main loop services peripheral writes through the same helpers immediately before the thermal worker. Quiescing only the thermal queue would not establish whole-transport ownership.

references.label: Main-loop peripheral writer before thermal worker
Peripheral write through the shared helper
Additional peripheral write through the shared helper

findings.title: Ready to dispatch is not exclusive access
findings.description: Command-report readiness, initialization phase and application-state checks do not compare transfer busy state, drain pending thermal work or acquire a transaction identity. Actual collision is not established.

references.label: Normal worker precedes later main-loop flag checks

findings.title: Application state 5 does not reserve the bus
findings.description: The recovered 00/04 value-5 branch changes application state and generic access only. Thermal queued work remains eligible; the peripheral writer also has transfer paths preceding or bypassing its state check. No main-context arbitrary-register queue or ownership token was established in the reviewed handlers. No actual collision is claimed.

findings.title: Application state is not a reversible ownership token
findings.description: The recovered setter stores the full input byte before comparisons with 1, 5 and 2. It resets without returning for 1 and changes auxiliary fields for 2; effects on entry to 3 or transition from 3 to 0 precede the store. It does not save prior auxiliary state. GET returns only the sampled byte. Replaying that byte supplies neither exact restoration nor a bus-drain acknowledgement; these are static findings, not admitted probe values.

references.label: GET returns the earlier state sample

findings.title: Parking entry and generic dispatch need incompatible state
findings.description: Initial entry to the reviewed parking path needs USB status bit 3 set and application state neither 3 nor 2. Timer generic dispatch needs state 3 or that bit clear. No unchanged state/bit combination admits both across all 256 bytes and both bit values. The parked loop can retry without resampling the application byte; this is an entry predicate, not a continuous invariant or exclusion of asynchronous transitions. No hardware collision is claimed.

findings.title: Normal-mode exit remains queued and needs independent confirmation
findings.description: The ordinary mode command caches a normal selector and manual flag, then queues work. With shared EC bank 0 selected, the worker writes mode and mailbox before arming a separate flag write; it does not itself force bank 0. Existing pending mode/manual reads can replace those same cached request bytes before their write branches; SET preserves the read bits. A matching cached GET does not prove that the EC left FE or reached Automatic. This is a conditional instruction-backed path, not an observed failed transition.

references.label: Pending mode read before mode write
Pending flag read before flag write
Conditional mode and flag read scheduling
